r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped direct dependencies for mobile-bff and portfolio-service, and listed recent infrastructure, configuration, and deployment changes across all services over the past 7 days.

findings.statement: mobile-bff has direct sync dependencies on auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, kyc-service, and aa-connector.
portfolio-service has direct sync dependencies on portfolio-db and market-data-service.
portfolio-service was deployed with v3.8.0 on 2026-10-08T18:20:00+00:00, introducing in-memory per-user holdings snapshots.
portfolio-db received a routine release deploy (v1.1.0) on 2026-10-09T12:27:00+00:00.

open_questions: What specific errors or error codes are being returned by portfolio-service and mobile-bff despite clean logs?

r1-observability-1.summary: Investigation into portfolio-service and mobile-bff confirms symptom onset at 13:43:00 UTC, matching error rate spikes and pod restarts. The SRE's observation of clean logs in portfolio-service is explained by the fact that portfolio-service ceased producing logs entirely after 13:37 alongside pod restarts, while mobile-bff captured upstream connection reset errors.

findings.statement: portfolio-service error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, peaking at 32.73%.
portfolio-service pod restarts anomaly started at 2026-10-09T13:42:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00, peaking at 10.23%.
mobile-bff logs show recurring upstream connection reset errors from portfolio-service starting at 2026-10-09T13:43:00+00:00.
portfolio-service produced zero logs after its last entry at 2026-10-09T13:37:38+00:00 during the incident window, explaining the clean-logs observation.

open_questions: What specific internal exception or condition caused portfolio-service to crash/restart and stop emitting logs without leaving a trace?

hypotheses.title: Portfolio-service memory exhaustion via in-memory per-user holdings snapshots (v3.8.0)
hypotheses.mechanism: Deployment chg-7001 introduced in-memory per-user holdings snapshots, which accumulated over time until reaching 99.8% memory saturation. This led to pod crashes and restarts starting at 13:42, stopping log emission at 13:37 and causing connection resets for mobile-bff at 13:43.

supporting.note: Introduced the in-memory holdings snapshots feature change on portfolio-service.
Shows portfolio-service memory is fully saturated at 99.8%.
Shows portfolio-service pod restarts spiking starting at 13:42.
Shows portfolio-service error rate spiking at 13:43.
Shows mobile-bff receiving connection reset errors from portfolio-service starting at 13:43.
Explains the clean-logs observation as portfolio-service ceased producing logs entirely after 13:37 during pod restarts.

contradicting.note: Reported as flat at 99.8% rather than showing a continuous gradual ramp-up leading directly to 13:42.

assumptions: Memory saturation at 99.8% triggers OOM killer or runtime crash leading to pod restarts and silence when holding cache grows over time.

hypotheses.title: Portfolio-db v1.1.0 release regression causing connection pool exhaustion or query deadlocks
hypotheses.mechanism: Routine release deploy v1.1.0 on portfolio-db introduced a breaking change or query regression, causing database requests from portfolio-service to hang or fail, eventually leading to cascading pod restarts.

supporting.note: Routine release deploy on portfolio-db occurred shortly before the incident onset at 12:27 on Oct 9.
Matches the timing of portfolio-service crashes following database issues.
Upstream connection resets correspond to downstream database dependency failures.

contradicting.note: Portfolio-service memory is at 99.8% saturation, directly pointing to in-memory caching changes rather than database response anomalies.

assumptions: The routine release deploy v1.1.0 on portfolio-db introduced a breaking query change or connection limit issue that manifests as abrupt pod crashes in portfolio-service.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: We established the exact symptom onset at 13:43 UTC via error rate spikes across portfolio-service and mobile-bff, with pod restarts beginning at 13:42 UTC. The SRE's observation of clean logs is fully explained by portfolio-service stopping log emission at 13:37 UTC due to crashes. Hypothesis H1 (memory exhaustion via in-memory holdings snapshots introduced in chg-7001) is strongly supported by 99.8% memory saturation and pod restarts, whereas H2 relies on a coincidentally timed database release (chg-9271) but lacks direct database metric anomalies.

adjustments.reason: Direct evidence shows portfolio-service memory is saturated at 99.8% (metric:portfolio-service:mem_pct), pod restarts began at 13:42, and log emission stopped at 13:37 explaining why logs appeared clean. Connection resets in mobile-bff start precisely at the onset (13:43).
Alternative hypothesis H2 is contradicted by the 99.8% memory saturation on portfolio-service which points squarely to the in-memory caching feature introduced in chg-7001.
